lane.before_the_unslotted_run: === gate lane status AT THE START of the unconditioned run ===
lane.before_the_slotted_attempt: gate lane: 1 of 1 slot(s) held (capacity from the default), 1 waiting
lane.policy: Gates are a reserved serial resource: the runs above were taken while other lanes held the lane, and their wall times are therefore an UPPER BOUND under contention, not clean numbers. The per-suite CPU figures are charged inside each suite's own process tree and are not a machine-wide count.

what: What the gate's per-phase and per-suite instrumentation actually observed, and the falsifications of the instrumentation itself. The complete cold/warm pair of one tree was NOT obtained inside this window: see "why_not" and "lane" below.

instrument.phase: scripts/lib/gate-phases.sh, called from scripts/test.sh at each phase boundary (instrumentation only; the same checks, order, verdict line, skip counts and exit codes)
instrument.suite: scripts/lib/gate-shims/{bash,node,powershell,wa} -> scripts/lib/gate-suite.mjs, one record per suite invocation into GATE_SUITES_JSONL
instrument.cpu: scripts/lib/gate-lane-sample.ps1 walks parent links from the suite's pid every 500 ms and sums user + kernel ticks (100 ns); a LOWER BOUND (a process that starts and exits between two samples contributes only what was seen; reported as null, never 0, when nothing was sampled)

measured.why_red: the first suite (scripts/test-parallel-finish.mjs, invoked from scripts/test.sh) asks the node-wide gate lane for a slot for its nested fixture gate; unslotted, the outer gate had no admission marker to pass down, so the fixture waited 722 s, was told it would run without a slot, and then failed its own check on the nested call's exit status (4294967295 !== 0) - scripts/test.sh is `set -e`, so the gate ended inside the build phase

reuse_refusal_observed.shows: a refusal is a named record, never a silence: the tree refusal names the reason and the recovery, the run falls back to a disposable clone, and a gate lane that grants no slot is terminal (exit 6, gate.ran=false) rather than a silent unslotted gate

why_not.clean_pair: A slotted cold/warm pair needs a gate-lane slot twice. The lane held 1 of 1 with a queue that ranged from 2 to 4 deep for the whole window (status quoted above); my queued request #151 sat at position 4 for 10 minutes and was cancelled to free the queue, and a later merge-lane attempt (#159) reached position 2 before this run was written up.
why_not.the_waiter_cost: Independently of my runs: a gate run without a slot pays the nested fixture's lane wait INSIDE itself (722 s measured above), which is the same 12-minute class of stall the owner saw in sibling lanes.
